author: Rahul kp
title: Ordinary vs
hook: count the votes, not the members!
simple_words: Ordinary needs more votes for than against. Special needs for-votes at least three times the against-votes.

definitions.meaning: Passed when votes cast in favour are ==more than== votes cast against, by members voting in person, by proxy or electronically.
Passed when votes in favour are ==at least three times== the votes against, and the notice states the intention to propose it as special.

key_points: Only votes actually cast are counted; !!abstentions and absentees are ignored!!
Special resolution majority is 3 times the votes against, not 75% of all members
Matters of routine business usually need an ordinary resolution
Fundamental changes, like altering the articles, need a special resolution

rows: For is at least 3 times against
Must state intent to propose as special

insight.text: Both majorities are measured on votes cast, so non-voters never change the result.

trick_hook: O = Over, S = Same times three

memory_trick.explanation: Ordinary needs just one more vote for than against. Special needs for-votes to be three times against-votes.

steps: Read the matter to be decided
Check the Act: ordinary or special?
Count votes cast for and against
Apply: For > Against, or For ≥ 3 × Against
exam_tip: In MCQs, if the option says majority of members present or on roll, it is wrong. The test is votes cast.

doubt.question: Are abstaining members counted as against?
doubt.answer: No. Abstaining members do not cast a vote, so they are in neither the for nor the against count.

mistakes.wrong: Special resolution needs 75% of all members on the register
mistakes.right: For-votes must be at least three times the against-votes, counted among votes cast.

mistakes.wrong: Ordinary resolution needs more than 50% of total members
mistakes.right: It needs only more votes for than against among votes cast.

mistakes.wrong: Abstention is treated as a vote against
mistakes.right: Abstention is not a vote; it is left out of both counts.

mistakes.wrong: Notice need not mention that a resolution is special
mistakes.right: The notice must state the intention to propose the resolution as a special resolution.

applicability: Companies Act 2013 as per ICMAI CAT material
reviewer_note: Dividend and articles examples are standard; confirm they match the ICMAI material's classification. No section numbers used.
check_notes: Writer: Dividend and articles examples are standard; confirm they match the ICMAI material's classification. No section numbers used.

Checker 1: Definition 1 (Ordinary Resolution): this leaves out parts of Section 114(1) of the Companies Act, 2013. The correct version is: votes cast in favour, including the chairman's casting vote if any, by members entitled to vote and voting on a show of hands, electronically or on a poll, in person or by proxy or by postal ballot, are more than the votes cast against. Add the casting vote and postal ballot.

Checker 1: Definition 2 (Special Resolution): add the third condition in Section 114(2). The intention is stated in the notice, the notice is duly given, AND the votes in favour (cast the same ways, including postal ballot) are at least three times the votes against.

Checker 1: trick_hook 'O = Over, S = Same times three': 'Same times three' makes no clear sense and does not match the memory trick that follows. Use something like 'O = One more, S = Simply three times (For ≥ 3 × Against)'.

Checker 1: Memory trick explanation 'just one more vote': on a poll, votes are counted by voting rights (shares), not by heads. Reword to 'votes in favour must exceed votes against (even by one vote)'.
Checker 1: Insight text 'non-voters never change the result': members who are present still count towards quorum, even if they don't vote. Qualify it to say they don't affect the majority count.
Checker 2: Memory trick 'O = Over, S = Same times three' is unclear. 'Same times three' does not say what is multiplied. Better: 'O = Over (For > Against); S = Smash it, For ≥ 3 × Against'.
Checker 2: Memory trick explanation 'Ordinary needs just one more vote' could be read as exactly one extra vote. Better: 'For-votes only need to exceed against-votes (even by one)'.

Checker 2: Definition 1 lists the modes of voting as in person, by proxy or electronically. Section 114 also covers postal ballot, and only members entitled to vote count. Better: 'members entitled to vote, in person, by proxy, by postal ballot or by electronic voting'.
